item.title: Opinion: Remembering Margo Howard
item.description: Margo Howard had a lot of life experience and used it to offer advice for years as "Dear Prudence" for Slate. She died this week at the age of 86.

item.title: How these slum dwellers went from one-room shacks to beautiful new apartments
item.description: It's a bold new experiment and it's already won a prize. Residents in a jam-packed slum, many of them living in one-room tin shacks, help design their apartments in a brand new building.

item.title: FDA weighs a new kind of flu shot based on technology RFK Jr. has questioned
item.description: The FDA is poised to render a decision on Moderna's mRNA-based flu shot, which could be the first of its kind to market. The decision is expected to reverberate throughout the biotech industry.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Lebanese who fled the Israeli invasion visit to see what's left
item.description: Residents of the ancient town of Nabatiyeh in southern Lebanon have endured wars in the past, but the latest conflict with Israel is testing the limits of their endurance.

item.title: More than 25,000 children lose previous legal protections, as federal contract ends
item.description: Thousands of unaccompanied immigrant children are set to lose legal representation. The federal contract that pays for legal access expired Friday.

item.title: Death toll in Spain border crisis reaches 67 as tens of thousands cross back in to Morocco
item.description: The death toll in Spain's Ceuta border crisis with Morocco has climbed to 67. They included some who drowned and some who were killed in a stampede to cross a breakwater barrier.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Why did OpenAI's and Anthropic's AI models hack other companies?
item.description: OpenAI and Anthropic say their models broke into other companies' systems during testing, raising security concerns amid a heated debate over how to regulate AI.

item.title: Over 81,000 U.S. soldiers are missing from past wars. One may soon be identified
item.description: In June, the Department of Defense disinterred the remains of an unidentified WWII soldier who had been buried in Sitka, Alaska for decades. Now, they'll try to confirm who he is.

item.title: Nurses chase Cyclospora using grocery receipts, food apps and detailed interviews
item.description: Public health nurses have been pulled from other duties in Washtenaw County, MI, to call hundreds of people sick with cyclosporiasis, and try to help them remember everything they ate in recent days.

item.title: Staff Sgt. Rampersad, 28, who always knew she wanted to serve, is laid to rest
item.description: Staff Sgt. Angel S. Rampersad is one of a handful of service members who've recently died in the conflict with Iran. Her family says she knew from a young age she wanted to serve in the military.
